record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Determine the integers n for which there exists a chiral 4-polytope whose right and left Petrie paths both have length n.

evidence.quote: Problem 12 Determine the integers n for which there exists a chiral 4-polytope with right and left Petrie paths of length n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract 4-polytope is a ranked partially ordered set (with ranks −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4) satisfying the standard axioms for abstract polytopes: it has a unique minimum and maximum element, every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly one element of each rank, it is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition (for any two elements F < G with rank(G) − rank(F) = 2, there are exactly two elements strictly between them). Such a polytope is called chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags, with adjacent flags lying in different orbits. For a chiral 4-polytope with base flag Φ, let σ_1, σ_2, σ_3 denote the distinguished generators of the rotation subgroup (where σ_i fixes all but the (i−1)- and i-faces of Φ). Define the right Petrie element as π_R = σ_1 σ_2 σ_3 and the left Petrie element as π_L = σ_1^{-1} σ_2 σ_3 (equivalently, the analogous element for the enantiomorphic image). The right (respectively left) Petrie length is the order of π_R (respectively π_L) in the rotation group; these are the lengths of the right and left Petrie paths of the polytope.

Determine all positive integers n for which there exists a chiral abstract 4-polytope whose right Petrie length and left Petrie length are both equal to n.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed among open problems in the theory of chiral polytopes. General theory notes that for chiral polytopes the left and right Petrie elements typically have different orders, and existing constructions (e.g., Coxeter's 1970 family) deliberately exploit differing lengths. No source found that resolves the existence question for chiral 4-polytopes where both Petrie lengths coincide and equal a given integer n.

status_evidence.title: Constructions for chiral polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: For chiral polytopes, the left- and right-Petrie polygons generally have different lengths.
status_evidence.claim: In chiral polytopes left and right Petrie lengths typically differ, motivating the question of when they can be equal.
